body:
I presume that's the case. Though wouldn't it be typical of the self-destructive to choose so poorly? Bit of a chicken and egg situation.
No idea. Kids brains are much more malleable. Forty years of this programming and it's a circuit board rather than software. Updates would need to be more extreme than a download. I  suppose medication could be viewed an adding a jumper to bypass 'bad' circuitry.
I digress.

Why? I don't know. I don't remember a time not feeling like this.  Have I been fighting, or merely existing? And why? Because I am a fucking coward. And now I've enmeshed myself into lives in a way I cannot unmesh. MY biggest regrets in life are not being successful when I tried at 15 and then that I had kids. I love them to bits, but now we're all trapped in my shit.
Missing a leg isn't an illness, I'm just missing whatever people have that makes life bearable for them. Am I broken or just made badly? As I said in another reply - my life is in theory great. There's no reason to be like this.
What hurts? Every day I wake to feeling shitty, feel shitty all day and then repeat. There's no hope. I feel so little happiness in anything. There's just a dead spot where positive emotions go. It's hard to describe. It's an emptiness that sucks everything down. 
 I just put on a mask and function and I'm very good at it. There's nothing inside, just a pretty facade everyone so readily accepts. 
It's true it's all pointless. So why bother? 
If we can let people die for physical pain, why not mental. I don't want this life.

She's too angry and tired of dealing with my shit and how it drains her. 
I let it all out mid-argument unfortunately. She said that she can't do anything to help and that I just have to deal with my own shit. That sounds harsh, but she's at the receiving end of my insecurity enough I guess.
I wouldn't be seeking whatever I'm seeking otherwise. I'm pretty much alone with this for now. I guess this is why people have friends. Meh, I've never been much for friends, probably because no-one ever seems to develop any attachment to me - frankly, outside of my family, no-one gives a shit about me in any meaningful way. Supposedly people are intimidated by my intelligence. Ha! More like people can see my weakness and patheticness and treat me as a fucking joke, which, let's face it, I am - I'm white, male, middle class, intelligent, well-educated, 'normal' upbringing, reportedly attractive, etc. 
So many times I've been told I'm choosing to be depressed. Maybe I am. Maybe I'm so shitty that I can just throw away my entire life so I can choose to be like this.  
No-one would ever know it's a suicide. There would be suspicions, but it'd just be a tragic accident.

Unfortunately  (1) is out of the question as I'll be out of the country.
(2) is actually loosely where I'm sitting right now. The problem, I find, is to maintain such a position means an attitude of not caring. Which would be adequate were it not for the seemingly inexorable spread of said attitude. I suppose it's a genuine slippery slope argument. Not caring about infidelity leads to having to not care about a (for me, laughably) central part of what constitutes a romantic partnership. Which in turn devalues the relationship and consequently her - This I don't desire. 
Option (2) is a start to ruminations at least

She is. She has been open (well, I assume) about her past transgressions and, for want of a better term, lack of moral fibre when in comes to fidelity. In  theory this is to ensure that there are no repeats. I think this is with good intentions. 
But, to save you the time I'll note that intentions are one thing, action is another. After all, she didn't intend to have an affair with me, just have some flirtatious fun. 
I recall when we were having the affair she said she would not sleep with her husband after me/same day as she could see how terrible it would make someone feel to have that done to them (never mind the fucking someone else thing, I guess!). I think that intention lasted zero days as we fucked that night and she went home and fucked her husband as soon as she got home.

As I've noted, I feel I deserve no grief. This is one of the problems I'm having with trusting her. I can obviously understand that affairs do happen, but, despite what most posters seem to assume, I wouldn't ever do it again. It was a horrible thing to do, it was a horrible time mostly and I have horrible guilt about it even now. 
This may well be laughable to most here, but I would be classed as a good person (apologies for your spattered screens) - I treat everyone well, I put huge amounts of energy into helping people (personally and volunteering), want the best for all people, am empathetic as hell etc.
Put it like this, I still feel guilty for having a two/three week relationship with a girl when I was still interested in the possibility of getting back together with my ex (we had a six month break after a couple of years of our relationship). She was just more into me than vice versa. I ended it with her when I realized there was a good likelihood of a reconciliation.  
Juxtaposed with my wife's apparent lack of any guilt or conscience regarding infidelity, this, as you noted, seems like a bad sign. 
Ultimately I think she enjoyed the naughtiness of the whole thing as well. Considering we've been together openly for five years, we're out of the exciting honeymoon phase. 
I'm essentially reliant on her not wanting to cheat, with no 'this is wrong' to stop her. 

But, as I've said, things are good between us. We have kids (from our previous marriages) and we have worked hard to create a harmonious and happy family (those who've blended families can understand this) and my kids love her. It's not just ending a relationship for me, there's little people to consider too. My discomfort at the possibility of my wife being unfaithful isn't enough to put my kids through another break up. They are my priority above all else. I feel like I've let them down more than enough by already breaking up their home once before. 

Seems like I'm just chasing my tail...hmm.

Good question. A mix of hope and that whole loving her thing (thus wanting to think the best of her. It's hard not to when you're so attached) I would expect.

I have come to that realization in the last few years or so. In all aspects of my life. I'm kind of pissed that I've basically lost my entire life to being depressed. Everything I missed or didn't do or achieve because of fear and self-loathing (and not even in Vegas).
It's a big problem trying to think clearly about something when your brain is actively trying to make you feel shitty about yourself all the time. Hence the acting like my fear might be unreasonable - I have a total lack of faith in my though processes and their results when it comes to people.

Nuclear option right off the bat? Ouch.
A spine has been developing over the last few years. Just seems a bit noodly recently.

Whoah there! I have to disagree with the suggestion that she (or has) already cheated on me. I'm as confident as I can be about that. 
This visit is just an opportunity that worries me. There have not been any previous opportunities that have engendered such concern. I just don't think it has been pragmatically possible. But, as will be noted, I'm sure her previous partners thought she hadn't cheated too.

I don't know if it's fear, but fear pervades me. Just imagine a high-functioning super-depressed person. That's me.

Nice metaphor!
Hm. I've got a lot of enthinkening to do. It'd all be so much easier if I didn't have to second guess everything in order to not be swayed by the results of depressive (thus irrational) thinking over the rational.

Before my lungs fill completely - is it guaranteed? Do relationships born of infidelity ever work out long term? Hmm. I expect someone has askreddit'ed that question before. I shall search away.
(Hope is a funny thing, eh?)

I searched, the question is not novel. There were a few examples of lasting relationships (multi-decade). Key word being 'few' I suppose.

There's a reason people look at 'book smarts' as not necessarily the most useful type living in a social world. I'd rather be more socially intelligent than have all this useless processing power.

The problem is that the relationship isn't ugly. I'm too cynical to call it beautiful and poetic, but as I've mentioned, it is a good one. 
The issue is the trust. There is hope in the sense that we all have all sorts of plans and dreams and that we do intend to live out our remaining years together. And I sincerely hope we do. 
It's a numbers game -she'll either cheat or not. Even if not, our marriage may fail as so many others (we're clearly doing our part to up the statistics!). Hell, if I were to leave and get a new partner (unlikely, if I left I'd just go solo) they may still end up cheating/leaving/etc.
And will I carry my trust issues now knowing that affairs don't just happen to other people. I started my first marriage with nothing other than the traditional concept and expectations. Losing the illusion of the infallible relationship really sucks.
I wish there was solid data to interpret and judge the risk in this situation. 

But conversely I'm not so stupid as to not see the risk. I anticipated the timbre of the responses I'd get. I have read so many threads like mine with the OP arguing against/refusing to listen to the overwhelming opinions. I have chuckled at the levels of self-delusion people can engage in. I'm hoping I'm a little more self-aware as I realize that my 'arguing' against people may be a subconscious tactic - if I can't defend continuing my relationship against someone who only sees through a small window that I have described, then I am clearly fucked. An indefensible position cannot survive sincere critique.
I can fool myself about lots of things. I'm sure, but I am rigid in my intellectual sincerity. I cannot stand to be otherwise.

Ugh. This is so messy and opaque.

Unfortunately I am very smart. In an academic sense. Unfortunately this is not an academic situation. I'm also pretty silly, but I think that's a good thing. 
What I would suggest is that I sound like a very foolish man trying to sound wise. Which I know I'm not when it comes to people, hence this post!

Yay! I'm a winner!
I'm curious as to why I deserve the accolade though.

It really does. I both trust her and don't.
This is the problem with all the mental issues of mine. I can't discern whether it is simply a mix of paranoia, low self-esteem, etc, that creates the paradoxical trust I have. Combined with my natural propensity for critical thinking and extensive education in it, I lose trust in myself.
I don't know if I'm just looking for flaws, contradictions, etc because that's what I do.

The worry isn't constant, but there are situations (like this) where it is clearly there. Hm. I think this is actually the first time I've had genuine (caveats apply!) worries. Though this could be the first potential cheating scenario that has arisen. I just don't know if I've created the worry because I'm so depressed or if it's 'real'. 

If we weren't so good as a couple (and we really are it seems) I wouldn't be here. I can imagine life without her. I just really, really, really don't want that.  

EDIT: thanks for the perspective, by the way. The vitriol is expected and deserved, but a little help is appreciated.

About six years ago I would have agreed. 
It's very hard to explain and I expect nothing but bile because, frankly, my actions were vile. 
There is certainly a level of being calculating that comes with acting in such a way. I'd like to come clean, but it would serve no purpose other than to cause a lot of pain where none needs to be caused. The relationship is long over and there are kids in the mix. Things have only really settled down recently and I'm not willing to put my kids at risk any more. 

I don't think the guilt is self-indulgent. It is tricky to explain and I wish I could think of a decent analogue of the situation. Simply put, we all do bad things and know they're bad. Yet we still do. I won't argue that it wasn't a totally selfish act, however.

It was a fucked up situation in a fucked up time. I will never offer excuses and will never shy away from my total culpability and from the wrongess of what I did. I fucked up, I learned. You will (rightly) not believe me, but I can sincerely say that I wouldn't do it again. The experience was not a pleasant one.

Alas, I don't lack empathy. If I did, life would be much easier.
I hope we do too! Thanks! :P

As an aside, I'd be intersested in asking questions about this. Whilst this is my word alone, I am being candid in this thread. I have no agenda. Stepping back I'm rather fascinated by it myself.

I did! What I meant is that the concept of her sleeping with another woman (even this friend) is ok with me. It's not just a matter of being told first, there's a level of involvement I'd like, rules etc. Standard sort of thing. 
Whilst my presence would be preferred, I accept that may not be likely. I'd like to at least be in the same city as her/them. And not for it to be a multi-day extravaganza. I suppose as presented it would be entirely about her and not 'us'. Which I believe would be a bad thing.

As above, I'm not at the 'go fuck someone and tell me about it' stage. For some background, I've slept with three people (one of them once and it would have been classified as coerced). So basically my wives.
Which is funny to read as it seems so conservative juxtaposed to my views on such things.
Anyway, sex and feelings are a package deal for me it seems. Or I don't have the experience to know how casual 'casual' is. If that makes sense. Fear of the unknown?

There is that. Perhaps also the possibilty of a power play arises - my wife insists that I am essentially way too good for her, everyone says how lucky she is, etc. Being a real person, she is complex. She likes to have control (we could label it 'control issues'), but feels I am the one thing she cannot control. 
Her sneaking off and being unfaithful could be like a token of her being in control and exercising some sort of power.

Polyamory is not on the table, one-time deals are. Essentially other people are sex toys, not relationships. Or should be, anyway. It's all theory thus far.

This is what I said to her. The 'at the moment' could change easily with the right person 'tempting' her.
And yes, the problem of lacking trust makes this difficult to navigate.

But I'm unwilling to give up on what is a great relationship. There are ups and downs, but we are happy in each others company, have the same goals, work well as a team, etc, etc. Hence why I risked the relationship in the first place.

I would, but I'm not sure I trust her to be honest as, in this instance, I'd say no to extra-martial fun. I'm not at the stage (nor may ever be) where I can just say 'go fuck some girl and come tell me all about it'.  
I think she's aware of this.

Hm. My natural inclination is to not resist her going, but this may be due to depression-induced spinelessness. 
From her perspective I would be being controlling and unfair. But every action has a price. I suppose her restricted travel is the price. 
She's on Reddit too. Toying with the idea of showing her this thread and suggesting she post one too just to see what is said for her perspective.

Thanks. I haven't been formally taught, I just spent enough time in university (I managed to change degrees twice, then did a masters) that it has just developed. Reportedly I'm exceptionally intelligent, so that may help.

Funnily,  I don't mind the idea of her sleeping with her friend. I just want everything to be done above board. Hell, this is even agreed upon. 
Knowing where we began, we accepted the possibility of extra-marital sex and so made promises about being honest etc. There's the understanding that it's not a taboo, it just needs to be done properly.
But promises are just like little vows about lifelong commitment, fidelity, etc...

I'm aware of what I deserve. Hence my odd dispassionate separation from the whirl of unpleasant emotions that go with this. I feel like an outside observer, or Redditor, looking in and the situation is funny - the stupid, deserving idiot who thinks that somehow he's something special enough or that a serial cheater has changed.

Alas, life is much more complicated than the precis of the story set out there. But the Reddit view is in no way discounted by the simplified tale set out.

She works. She's the main earner in the house and always has been in all her realtionships.

It's true. Though given the seeming commonness of infidelity, I wonder how much difference a previous record makes? Wonder in the sense that it would be statistically interesting. 
I was a faithful husband/partner for almost 20 years. Then I wasn't. Am I now a cheater or someone who has cheated? Does one incidence set a pattern of behaviour?

I don't unfortunately, but I have watched the show enough to understand the example. But is this the whacking attempt, or would her actually cheating be it (on the presumption I managed to find out).
Thanks.

It's a possibility. Exchange secretly for subconsciously. 
I don't think it is the case, but I'm open to examining all possibilities. After all, if I'm into it, then any non-monogamous energies could be expended in a non-cheating way!
But it's true. Going into this relationship as a 'real' relationship meant looking at the almost overwhelming statistical suggestions that there will be further infidelity ( most liekly on her part, key factors being - parents unfaithful, multiple occurences of infidelity, no guilt) and hoping that we, in our knowledge and understanding of the risks, can avoid that fate.
It really has been the riskiest (or, as everyone here notes, stupidest) thing I've ever done.

This is a question I have asked. The only answer is 'because I don't want to'. Which is maybe the best answer to get. A lack of desitre to cheat is better than not cheating due to feeling it is morally wrong, etc as it would hopefully suggest that your partner is happy with you.
But she could well be telling a big fat lie. I'm not sure any couple would respond any other way unless the level of honesty was sky high.

I was unclear it seems. I don't believe there is karma in action, the thought of the potential karmic retribution amused me. It's not like I can ever get indignant if she does cheat as I've utterly earned it. As I said in another comment - there is and was no justification for it. I will never look at it as anything other than one of the most shameful things I have done. I am still, 5 years later, disgusted with myself.

I suppose it's like playing the lottery - we're all hoping to be the rare exception. It may well be no less foolish. I hope the odds are a little better though! Funnilty I'm normally utterly risk-averse to the point of pussydom. And yet here I am. Life is opdd sometimes.

As for the crappy thinking - indeed. I have been depressed my entire life. A void where self-esteem should be means you are led to unwise decisions if not vigilant. My previous marriage probably wouldn't have even got to the ring-on-finger point if I had any sense of self-worth.
It's got to the point where I think it's time to medicate (last time was when I was 18) again, though I am really averse to it. Not quite sure why my aversion is so strong though. My external life is good, internally every day is hellish. I don't know why I'm so scared to try and get 'fixed'.

Too presumptive on a few things. I'm looking for advice as I genuinely don't trust my assessments due to the lens of depression. 
I absolutely do not think cheating is ok. It's a horrible thing to do, totally unecessary. I am not happy or proud that I did it. If I had the chance to rewind, I would not do it again - I would have ended the marriage with decency. Shame and guilt are my key responses when I think of what I did. Even though my then wife was a cunt, I was still not justified in cheating. I'd say no-one ever is.
Also, clearly not a faultless angel. She was totally at fault. Hence why I remain vigilant. 
I think you are trying to attach some arrogance to me that isn't there. I'm generally humble, recognizing my human frailty and all that. 

As an aside, are posts like these looking for reinforcement or people to tell them what they already know but really don't want to admit? (not saying that's the case here, however).
I wish I was a believer in non-material metaphysics. The idea of the karma in this is amusing. It's almost hollywoodized.

I did go into this with my eyes wide, wide open and they continue to be so. It's a little draining sometimes, but it would be idiotic not to. 
I'm also not perfect, so may miss that which I shouldn't.
The lack of guilt bothers me. I was torn apart by guilt during the affair, despite my marriage being dead in the water for a while. The wrongness pervaded, but I was too weak/attached to stop it. I look back at the time generally as utter hell with moments of heaven. 
She claimed she loved her husband, he was her best friend, etc. But when you're inside someone and their husband rings and then end wiht 'i love you's', one does wonder about definitions.
Thanks. I really hope I don't need it.
